options.A: Birds other than partridges that live in or around cereal crop fields have also been suffering population declines.

options.C: The elimination of certain weeds from cereal crop fields has reduced the population of the small insects that live on those weeds and that form a major part of partridge chicks' diet.
options.D: The toxins contained in herbicides typically used on cereal crops can be readily identified in the tissues of animals that have ingested them.

problem.passage: Hydraulic fracturing is an oil and gas well stimulation measure with wide application prospect. This method uses the surface high-pressure pump to squeeze and inject fracturing fluid with high viscosity into the oil layer through the wellbore, press the oil layer open and produce fractures, so as to establish a new fluid channel between the oil layer and the wellbore, The production of oil and gas wells will generally increase greatly. But this technology will bring great damage to the environment.
problem.question: Which of the following arguments can lead to the above conclusion?

options.A: When the injection rate of fracturing fluid exceeds the absorption capacity of the oil layer, the oil layer at the bottom of the well will form a high pressure.
options.B: In order to ensure that the pressed crack will not close, it is necessary to inject displacement fluid into the crack and support it.
options.C: The development of oil and gas fields will affect the lives of nearby residents, and the pipeline for residential water needs to bypass the location of the wellbore.
options.D: Injecting high-strength fracturing fluid below the surface may activate dormant geological faults and trigger earthquakes.

problem.passage: Until recently, endosulfan was one of the most widely used pesticides. Some others -- toxaphene, dieldrin, and chlordane -- were banned or restricted in many countries in the 1980s but linger in the environment. All four have a weak effect individually in increasing estrogen levels in women. Scientists have found, however, that their potential to cause health hazards increases dramatically when the chemicals are combined. For example, a mixture of endosulfan and dieldrin had 160 to 1, 600 times more estrogen-boosting potency than either chemical did individually. Increased estrogen is associated with an increased cancer risk in women.
problem.question: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

options.D: Because of its hazards when combined with other chemicals, endosulfan is more dangerous than most other pesticides.

problem.passage: Before making a decision, if the value of each thing is roughly similar in the minds of decision makers, it is difficult to determine its advantages and disadvantages. However, after making a choice, the decision-makers' attitude and evaluation of these things have changed. This phenomenon is called post decision effect.
problem.question: According to the above definition, which of the followings is a post decision effect?

options.A: A staff member was unable to manage his own stay. After considering it, he thought that he had to face many complicated relationships to stay.
options.B: A woman was difficult to choose between two brands of mobile phones with their own advantages and disadvantages. Finally, she chose one of them from an economic point of view, but she found that this one had color difference after arrival.
options.C: A teacher hesitated to choose A or B to participate in the competition. The monitor suggested choosing B. Afterwards, the teacher thought that choosing B was completely correct, because B finally won the championship.
options.D: A student hesitated to apply to university A or university B when filling in his volunteer. Finally, he followed the teacher's advice and chose A. from then on, he felt that A was better than B.

Option C clearly demonstrates the change in evaluation after the decision.  
FINAL_ANSWER: C

problem.passage: When a forest is subject to acid rain, the calcium level in the soil declines. Spruce, fir, and sugar maple trees all need calcium to survive. problem.question: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the greater decline among sugar maples?

options.A: Unlike spruces or firs, most sugar maples are native to areas that receive a lot of acid rain.
options.B: Spruces and firs, unlike sugar maples, can extract calcium from a mineral compound that is common in soil and is not affected by acid rain.
options.C: Sugar maples require more calcium in the spring and summer than they do in the fall and winter.
options.D: Sugar maples that do not receive enough calcium deteriorate less rapidly than spruces or firs that do not receive enough calcium.
